en.title: Fortnite Treasure Hunters Drops New Anime Gear and Vaults Old Favorites
en.summary: Fortnite's latest season, Treasure Hunters, has officially landed, shaking up the island's loot pool with a wave of anime-inspired weaponry and items. Players will need to adapt quickly as familiar tools are removed to make way for these exciting new additions.
en.body:
Fortnite's ever-evolving island has once again been refreshed with the launch of the **Treasure Hunters** season, bringing a vibrant new loot pool that leans heavily into popular anime aesthetics. This latest update, version 43.00, introduces a substantial collection of 11 new weapons and items, many of which are inspired by beloved anime franchises, most notably **One Piece**. Players can now wield powers like the **Gum-Gum Fruit** and **Flame-Flame Fruit**, or even master **Zoro's Three Sword Style**, offering entirely new ways to engage in combat and traverse the map.

Beyond the direct anime tie-ins, the **Treasure Hunters** season also sees the return of some fan-favorite unvaulted items, ensuring a mix of the familiar and the novel. However, this influx of new gear comes at a cost. In a move that will undoubtedly alter early-game strategies and resource management, **Gold Bars** have been vaulted, and **Vending Machines** have been removed from the island entirely. This means players will need to rely more on traditional looting and combat for their gear, making each encounter and chest discovery all the more crucial.

## A Pirate's Bounty of New Gear

The full list of new additions is extensive and promises to inject fresh excitement into every match. Alongside the aforementioned **Gum-Gum Fruit**, **Flame-Flame Fruit**, and **Zoro's Three Sword Style**, players can get their hands on **A$AP Rocky's Shock Rocket**, **Usopp's Slingshot**, the **Bundlebuss Repeater Rifle**, and the **Gilded Dragoon Shotgun**. Utility items also get a boost with the **Explosive Cannon Ball**, **Nami's Tangerine**, and **Meat on a Stick**. A particularly intriguing rare drop is the **Pirate Shop token**, which grants two 14-day windows of access to the Item Shop, a unique reward for dedicated explorers.

## What This Means for Players

This significant overhaul of the loot pool is more than just a cosmetic update; it's a fundamental shift in how players will approach matches. The removal of **Gold Bars** and **Vending Machines** forces a re-evaluation of farming routes and economic strategies. Players who previously relied on purchasing specific weapons or utility items will now need to adapt to a more RNG-dependent system. The anime-themed items, in particular, offer potent abilities that could define the meta for this season. Mastering their usage and understanding their limitations will be key to achieving victory. The **Fortnite Treasure Hunters** season is a clear signal from Epic Games that they are committed to keeping the game fresh and exciting by constantly introducing new mechanics and collaborations that appeal to a broad, passionate fanbase.

## What's Next

As is typical with Fortnite seasons, the loot pool is expected to evolve. Epic Games often introduces new items or unvaults more weapons as the season progresses, so players should stay vigilant and adapt to any changes. The developers have not yet announced specific mid-season updates, but the current array of treasures offers plenty to discover.

content_raw: One of the most exciting aspects of each new Fortnite season is the updated loot pool, which consistently brings fresh items to the island while also rotating back in old favorites. In Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters season, the loot pool has plenty to discover. Discovering and keeping track of everything available to find around the island is essential, as certain items are sure to work better for your combat style than others. If you want to keep up with everything that’s up for grabs, here’s all of the weapons and loot you can find around the island in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.
